design.shape: presence + denial, not a table of known-good phrasings
design.presence: ATTRIBUTION_EFFECT (window truncat / compaction-window / steady-state truncat / truncation *plus*) AND ATTRIBUTION_NEGATION (not ... break|fork|append cost) within +/-6000 chars of every 1.700x / 1.7002x / 1.70x statement
design.window_measurement: measured, not guessed: abstract figure-to-attribution distance 1,077 chars (one paragraph); CLAIMS.md C21/C24 row to C44 row 5,034-5,171 chars because the table is column-aligned; 6,000 is wider than the table padding and still narrower than the distance to any unrelated attribution
denials: DENY-1 the 1.700x / the win *is* a break-cost effect
DENY-2 avoiding / skipping / never creating the break *saves* the prefix or tokens
DENY-3 forking instead of compacting *preserves* the prefix
DENY-4 not compacting *is what buys* the 1.700x
DENY-5 compacting less often *saves* prefix tokens
DENY-6 the figure framed as resting on the break (is what / is bought / rests on)
design.no_bare_noun_rule: 'break' appears legitimately throughout (MANUSCRIPT.md's SS 6 table column is 'Net break cost'), so only assertions are findings
design.negation_exemption: a DENY match whose own sentence negates it is not a finding, so G1's corrective wording 'the 1.700x is post-compaction window truncation, not break-event cost' does not read as the claim it corrects
design.historical_quotes: exempt via double-quoted spans -- the marker CLAIMS.md already uses ('U15: "avoiding the break saves the prefix"' in Corrections row 7, and Supersessions by G1); no new/invisible syntax invented
design.scope: causal claims only; inline code spans (cards, files, claim ids) are skipped
